I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life, same as my father did. The soil here on the North China Plain is what I know. There's no question in my mind — I plant winter wheat and summer maize, same as always. That double-crop rotation is what everyone around here does, and it's what I know how to do well.

My family farms about 8 mu. After wheat is harvested in June, the maize goes in right away on the same ground. I don't waste land.

For wheat, I'll use a variety like Jimai 22 — it's been reliable for years and the seed station nearby carries it. I put down plenty of fertilizer before sowing and top-dress at jointing. Water is the worry in spring — I'll flood-irrigate at least three times, more if it's dry. I spray herbicide early, then watch for aphids and rust closer to heading.

For maize, I'll go with Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, it's what most people around here use and the yield is good. I broadcast urea at planting and again at V6 or so. Maize doesn't need as much water — one or two irrigations if rain is short. I'll spray once for pests if I see anything.

I use rotary tillage before wheat planting — that's what I've always done. For maize, I just direct-seed into the stubble after combining the wheat. Saves time.
